sources.title: BNaR digitized archival inventory: Iurghiceni documents, 1591–1592, 1611 and 1619; separate 1599 court judgment

1611: Frim son of Bilan sells his Iurghiceni ocină to his nephew Costinovici
1611 I/18: the BNaR inventory explicitly calls Costinovici a vistier (treasurer/treasury official), not merely a person bearing the name Costinovici
sources.independence: Primary archival catalogue; catalogue adjacency does not establish person or family continuity. Individual document contents must be inspected.
sources.notes: BNaR inventory establishes I/14 (1591–1592) as a genuine Iurghiceni transaction: Ștefan son of Cătrîna, grandson of priest Gavril, sells his Iurghiceni share from the Băsărăbești side to his cousin Obrejie, son of Agafia and grandson of priest Gavril, for 40 zlotys. The verso is annotated 'Cost. Paladi hatm.' This is an archival annotation/verso note, not evidence that the 1591–1592 transaction was authored by the later Constantin Paladi. The same caution applies to later BNaR items carrying a Paladi verso/author field: chronology must come from the underlying document, not the later annotation alone.

sources.title: Documenta Romaniae Historica A. Moldova, vol. V (1621–1625), doc. 129 — Gligorie and his brother Costin of Iurghiceni
supports: 6 January 1622: Ștefan Tomșa confirms Gligorie and his brother Costin, vistiernicei from Iurghiceni, their jointly purchased share of Arvasia, daughter of Marco, granddaughter of Gage, bought from Umbrar vataf of Rădeni for 35 silver talers
sources.independence: Scholarly edition of the documentary record; primary-document transcription.

sources.title: Documenta Romaniae Historica A. Moldova, vol. XXI (1632–1633), doc. 22 — Gavril and Gligorie, sons of Palaghia, Iurghiceni
supports: 17 April 1632: Gavril and his brother Gligorie, sons of Palaghia and grandchildren of Miron, sell their Iurghiceni hereditary holding to Iachim Bandur
sources.independence: Primary-document transcription in a scholarly edition.
sources.notes: The 17 April 1632 original says Gavril and his brother Gligorie, sons of Palaghia and grandsons of Miron, sold their hereditary holding from the fourth part of Iurghiceni. The phrase also refers to their share being selected from the shares of 'other brothers', showing that the sibling group was larger than the two named here. This means the 1622 Gligorie's brother Costin cannot be ruled out solely because Costin is not named in the 1632 sale; however, the 1632 document does not identify Costin as a son of Palaghia.

sources.title: Documenta Romaniae Historica A. Moldova, vol. V (1621–1625): 6 January 1622 paired Costin–Grigore/Gligorie records

sources.independence: Scholarly documentary edition. The paired entries provide a strong textual variant/identity clue for Grigore/Gligorie, subject to checking the printed pagination and original documents.

sources.title: BNaR finding aids: later Iurghiceni records involving Costin; Vasco–Costin–Iacob
supports: BNaR item 3357: multiple Iurghiceni villagers attest to Costin's holding
BNaR item 3444 (inventory cotă I/135): 'Părțile de moșie din Iurghiceni ale fraților Vasco, Costin, Iacob, ce trebuie să se aleagă…'; the verso is noted as 'Constantin Paladi hatman'
BNaR item 3445: Iurghiceni shares from the Băsărăbești side
sources.independence: Archival finding aid; individual undated entries require recovery of the underlying scans before chronological placement.
sources.notes: Important chronological correction: item 3444 is NOT safe to use as evidence for the 1611–1632 Costin. BNaR marks its date as [s.d.] and the verso names Constantin Paladi hatman. Independent historical literature identifies hatman Constantin Paladi as a late-18th/early-19th-century figure who died in 1831. Therefore item 3444 is currently a much later finding aid/document and must be kept separate from the 17th-century Costin until its exact date and provenance are established. Item 3357 also requires recovery and dating before use.

sources.title: Documenta Romaniae Historica A. Moldova, vol. XXV (1639–1640), docs. 173 and 187 — Obrejie and the Băsărăbești share of Iurghiceni
supports: 15 July 1639: Irina, daughter of Mărica Nehoe and granddaughter of Băsărabă, and Niță vătaf sell to Obrejie, son of Agahia and nephew of priest Gavril, their Iurghiceni share from the Băsărăbești family for 50 zlotys
22 July 1639: Vasile son of Andrieca and Costantin son of Ana, grandsons of Borcea, sell to Obreje, son of Agahia, their Iurghiceni share from the Băsărăbești family for 35 zlotys
sources.independence: Scholarly edition of primary documentary records.

sources.title: Documenta Romaniae Historica A. Moldova, vol. XXIII (1637–1638), doc. 110 — two Obrejie identities at Iurghiceni
supports: 26 May 1637: Obrejie of Iurghiceni, son of Miron, appears with other Iurghiceni răzeși in a collective testimony
26 May 1637: a separate Obrejie, son of Lupu, is also named from Iurghiceni in the same record
1637 demonstrates that multiple distinct Obrejie identities existed at Iurghiceni
sources.independence: Scholarly edition of primary documentary record.
sources.notes: This source is important for deduplication. The 1637 record explicitly distinguishes Obrejie son of Miron from Obrejie son of Lupu. Neither is identified as the son of Agahia/Agafia. Therefore the 1639 Obrejie son of Agahia should not be merged with either 1637 Obrejie without additional evidence.

sources.title: Documenta Romaniae Historica A. Moldova, vol. XXVII (1643–1644), doc. 459 — Miron of Iurghiceni and deceased son Obrejie
supports: 28 November 1644: Miron of Iurghiceni donates his share of Iurghiceni for the soul of his deceased son Obrejie
The record identifies a distinct Miron–Obrejie parent-child relationship at Iurghiceni in 1644
sources.independence: Scholarly edition of a primary documentary record.
sources.notes: This Obrejie is not automatically the 1639 Obrejie son of Agahia, nor the 1637 Obrejie son of Miron or son of Lupu. The record instead establishes a separate Miron–Obrejie family clue requiring identity comparison.

sources.title: Documenta Romaniae Historica A. Moldova, vol. XXVIII (1645–1646), doc. 43 — Obrejie and Miron of Iurghiceni
supports: 31 March 1645: Obrejie and Miron of Iurghiceni appear as named local witnesses to the transfer of a Iurghiceni holding by Pavăl Băzarca and Cozma Duma
The record places Obrejie and Miron together in the same Iurghiceni community in 1645
sources.independence: Scholarly edition of a primary documentary record.
sources.notes: This record does not give Obrejie's patronymic and therefore cannot by itself identify him as the 1639 Obrejie son of Agahia or the deceased son of Miron in the 1644 record. It is useful as a chronological/community continuity marker only.

sources.title: Documenta Romaniae Historica A. Moldova, vol. XXIV (1637–1638), doc. 410 — Iurghiceni Doșcești branch and Agafia

sources.notes: Identity-control evidence. The Agafia in this 1638 Doșcești-side title chain is not to be equated with the Agafia/Agahia named as Obrejie's parent in the 1591–1592 and 1639 Băsărăbești-side records without explicit kinship or property evidence.

sources.independence: External aggregated surname database; useful as a benchmark and research lead, not treated as a census or authoritative population count.
sources.notes: The current page reports approximately 399 people bearing the surname, with 212 in Romania, 148 in Turkey, 17 in the United States, 9 in Indonesia, 7 in India, and 1 each in Brazil, Cyprus, England, Peru and Slovenia; it separately reports Çiçan and notes that Cican may also occur as a forename. HOUSE OF CICAN records these figures as an external estimate to audit rather than as established fact. Internal consistency check: the visible country incidence values listed on the current page sum to 398, while the headline says approximately 399 and the page says Cican occurs in 11 countries (Romania plus 10 others), whereas the visible table in the captured result lists Romania plus 9 other countries. HOUSE OF CICAN records this discrepancy for verification rather than attempting to reconcile it by assumption.

sources.title: Un popor care se stinge, 1915 — Nicolae Cican and Spiru Cican in Corcea
supports: Nicolae Cican as a banker in Corcea

Spiru Cican as Nicolae's brother and tenant
Dina Cican contemporary testimony
financial/property loss context
sources.independence: Contemporary published testimony/report; strong identity-context evidence, but exact publication provenance and underlying original testimony should be documented further.
sources.notes: The source reproduces Nicolae Cican's signed statement after his house was burned, identifies him as a banker, and explicitly states that Spiru Cican was his brother and tenant. This is high-value bridge evidence for the Nicolae/Spiru cluster and should be kept distinct from any unsupported relationship among other 1903 Cicans. The publication's compensation table independently lists Nicolae Cican, Dina Cican and Spiru Cican among Romanians of Corcea with recorded losses from the 23 March 1914 violence. This establishes that all three were individually affected/documented in the same contemporary administrative context, while the source's explicit sibling statement remains limited to Nicolae and Spiru.

sources.independence: Official BNaR archival inventory; the inventory descriptions do not themselves identify Cican in these entries.
sources.notes: This cluster is potentially valuable for backward reconstruction because it explicitly says the 1673 boundary/share lists derive from purchase deeds. The underlying undated list may preserve older deeds, but Cican/Illea has not yet been recovered from the list itself. Treat as a high-value retrieval target, not as evidence of Cican continuity.
sources.verification_update: BNaR digitization inventories dated January 2025 and March 2026 independently list I/227 and I/228 among digitized documents. This confirms scan availability/status in the BNaR digitized-document program, but the public inventory does not expose the scan contents; no Cican/Illea name has therefore been extracted from I/227 or I/228 yet.

sources.title: 22 July 1643 order to bring old Iurghiceni deeds for boundary investigation
sources.publisher: Documenta Romaniae Historica, Seria A, Moldova, vol. XXVII (1643–1644)
supports: Vasile Lupu orders the inhabitants of Iurghiceni and Tălhărești to bring all old documents to a boundary investigation of parts of those villages
The order demonstrates that older title documents for Iurghiceni were still being used/expected in 1643
sources.independence: Published documentary edition; the underlying princely order is primary evidence, while this online copy is a secondary access point.
sources.notes: This is a critical bridge for the archival strategy. It does not name Cican/Cicican, but proves that an inventory of older deeds existed/was expected for boundary reconstruction in 1643. The 1673 I/227–I/229 cluster can therefore be pursued as a possible later preservation/listing of such title documents.

sources.title: BNaR archival sequence I/3–I/5: 1497–1547 gap control for Iurghiceni
supports: I/3: 1497 Stefan cel Mare document concerning a different property purchase by Drăguș Carîmbu
I/4: 1498 Milcinești boundary charter
I/5: 26 May 1547 Iliaș confirms Cican and his son at Iurghiceni
sources.independence: Official BNaR inventory; absence between catalogued items is not proof of documentary absence from Moldova.
sources.notes: The BNaR sequence around the Cican charter does not provide an earlier Iurghiceni/Cican item: the immediately preceding catalogued records are 1497 and 1498 records for other places, followed by I/5 in 1547. This strengthens the archival-search benchmark but does not prove 1547 was the first ever Cican occurrence.

sources.title: BNaR I/127–I/151: additional undated Iurghiceni documentary cluster
supports: I/127: Andonic and Acsinia, children of Dumitrașco from Iurghiceni, sell their estate
I/128: Maximiam the ban pledges a part of Iurghiceni estate to logofăt Buhuş
I/137: list of confirmations/documents concerning Iurghiceni estate
I/146: Ilie son of Vasile from Iurghiceni sells his hereditary share in Iurghiceni
I/150: Stefav Voievod empowers Nicolae Buhuş to send someone to Iurghiceni
I/151: Ștefan Voievod notice concerning Iurghiceni
sources.independence: Official BNaR inventory. These entries are retrieval targets and do not establish Cican continuity.
sources.notes: These entries may contain recited older purchase deeds or ownership history. The undated status prevents chronological placement without inspecting the underlying documents. I/137 is especially relevant because it is explicitly a list of documentary confirmations for the Iurghiceni estate.

sources.title: BNaR Iurghiceni property dossier, 1657–1669: Buhuş acquisitions, local owners and boundary records
supports: 1657 Ionașco Bandurul gives Nicolae Buhuş his Iurghiceni share
1657 Gheorghe Ștefan Voievod confirms Nicolae Buhuş's Iurghiceni share
1660–1663 Irimia son of Mănăilă sells his Iurghiceni share to Buhuş
1661 preotul Simion sells multiple Iurghiceni ancestral/property portions to Nicolae Buhuş
1669 Iachim sells his Iurghiceni share to Dumitrașcu Buhuş
1669 Constantin son of Vasile of Iurghiceni, grandson of Vasco cel bătrân, appears in an Iurghiceni property transaction
1669 Tudosie Dubău records selection and boundary work concerning Iurghiceni
sources.independence: Official BNaR digitized-document inventory; inventory descriptions are evidence of document existence/content summaries, not substitutes for inspecting the underlying manuscripts.
sources.notes: This cluster materially strengthens the property-chain investigation between the 1547 Cican/Illea purchase and the 1673 register. It does not identify Cican/Illea in these later records and must not be treated as proof of continuity. Particularly useful targets are I/141–I/142 (1657), I/151 and I/153–I/156 (1660–1661), and I/214 (1669).

sources.title: Documenta Romaniae Historica, A. Moldova, vol. XXI (1632–1633): Iurghiceni documents, 17 April 1632
sources.publisher: Academia Republicii Socialiste România / archival edition
sources.source_type: critical documentary edition of primary acts
supports: Andronic and Irimia pledge their Iurghiceni share to Iachim Bandur
Iurghiceni villagers attest to giving Costin's share to Bandur for payment of Costin's tax
Gavril and Gligorie, sons of Palaghia and grandsons of Miron, sell their share from a fourth part of Iurghiceni to Iachim Bandur for 20 zlotys
sources.notes: The 17 April 1632 cluster is a major property-chain control for Iurghiceni. It demonstrates that shares were being described by fractions and inherited family branches decades before the 1673 register. It does not identify Cican/Cicican or Illea and therefore does not establish continuity with the 1547 charter. The documentary edition identifies the acts as nos. 20–22; secondary searchable reproduction preserves the original text and archival shelfmarks.

sources.title: Documenta Romaniae Historica, A. Moldova, vol. XXIV (1637–1638), Iurghiceni title chain
sources.publisher: Academia Republicii Socialiste România / archival edition
sources.source_type: critical documentary edition of primary acts
supports: 26 April 1638: Bandur's Iurghiceni property is described as purchased by Bandur from Baltag
14 July 1638: Iachim Bandur sells the Iurghiceni property to Dumitru Buhuș
The 14 July act identifies Baltag's purchase from Ion and Constantin, sons of Sidor and Agafia, plus Zaharia Benea/Banea and his nephews Vasile and Tudora
The property is identified as the upper half of Iurghiceni, the Doșcești portion, excluding a smaller Flora portion on the Bahlui
sources.notes: This is a documentary title chain, not a genealogical chain. It reaches one generation of named prior sellers before Baltag and provides precise fractional/geographic property identifiers. It does not connect any of these owners to the 1547 Cican/Cicican and Illea charter.

sources.title: BNaR I/214, 30 November 1669: Constantin son of Vasile, grandson of Vasco cel Bătrîn
sources.source_type: archival inventory entry for original Romanian deed
supports: Constantin, son of Vasile of Iurghiceni and grandson of Vasco cel Bătrîn, sells an Iurghiceni share to Ianache vornicul
The share had been pledged to Benea by Constantin's uncle David
sources.notes: Benea is a potentially important name collision with Zaharia Benea/Banea in the 1638 Iurghiceni title chain. The present evidence does not establish that the 1669 Benea is the same person, family branch, or creditor line as the 1638 Zaharia Benea/Banea. The Vasco branch is also not connected to Cican/Illea.

sources.title: Documenta Romaniae Historica, A. Moldova, vol. XXIV, 27 July 1640: Iurghiceni title dispute
sources.publisher: Academia Republicii Socialiste România / archival edition
sources.source_type: critical documentary edition of primary judicial act
supports: Băltag's Iurghiceni acquisition is stated in court as purchased from Benea and other relatives
Bandur's widow alleged the 1638 transaction was a pledge rather than a sale
Dumitru Buhuș produced Bandur's deed and other princely/official documents
The court rejected the widow's claim and left her without legal standing
sources.notes: This is materially stronger than the 1638 transaction alone because a 1640 judicial proceeding tests the title chain and explicitly identifies Benea and relatives as the prior sellers to Băltag. It still does not connect Benea/Baltag/Bandur to the 1547 Cican/Cicican–Illea parcel.

sources.title: BNaR Iurghiceni documentary inventory cross-check, 1638–1640 title-chain records
supports: BNaR catalog preserves separate 1638 Iurghiceni transactions involving Iachim Bandur and later Dumitru Buhuș
BNaR catalog preserves a 1640 Iurghiceni judicial/ownership record involving Buhuș and the Bandur estate
The 1638–1640 cluster is suitable for tracing title documents and parcel identity before attempting any Cican/Illea continuity claim
sources.notes: Inventory metadata is used here as an archival control, not as a substitute for recovering the full manuscript text. The present investigation requires the actual underlying acts or critical edition before identifying exact kinship or boundary continuity.

sources.title: BNaR digitized Iurghiceni chain: I/62, I/68, I/70–I/73, I/76, I/78
supports: I/62: 14 July 1634 testimony of 14 boyars that Iachim Banduru sold Buhuș a part of Iurghiceni
I/68: c.1635 note in Slavonic and Romanian concerning shares and inhabitants of Iurghiceni
I/70: 26 May 1637 deed in which Iurghiceni răzeși pledge land to Buhuș
I/71: 2 April 1638 princely order concerning Buhuș holding pledged Iurghiceni shares
I/72: 20 April 1638 order to select pledged Iurghiceni shares for Buhuș
I/73: 26 April 1638 confirmation to Buhuș of a part of Iurghiceni bought from Bandur
I/76-a/b: 1638 Bandur-to-Buhuș Iurghiceni transaction, original Slavonic plus Romanian translation
I/78-a/b: 27 July 1640 confirmation to Buhuș of the Iurghiceni part bought from Bandur after litigation, with Romanian translation
sources.notes: This sequence materially improves the chronological control of the Bandur/Buhuș title chain. The BNaR inventory confirms digitization of the key 1638 and 1640 documents, but the public inventory itself does not expose manuscript images. Exact parcel continuity with the 1547 Cican/Cicican–Illea share remains unproven.

sources.title: BNaR I/9–I/10, 2 August 1575: Drăghici's Iurghiceni estate
supports: I/9: Petru Vv. confirms Condrea half of Drăghici's estate, purchased for 60 Tatar zlotys; the land is stated to have been acquired from Ștefan Vv. cel Bătrân by Drăghici's grandfather Toader
I/10: Petru (Șchiopul) confirms Burlan and Nikita, sons of Drăgan, half of Drăghici's estate in Iurghiceni on the Bahlui
sources.notes: This is a major post-1547 Iurghiceni ownership control. It proves an Iurghiceni estate held by Drăghici was being divided in 1575 and that its title was traced to an earlier acquisition by his grandfather Toader from Ștefan cel Bătrân. It does NOT establish that this Toader was Toader son of Maria from the 1547 Cican/Cicican transaction, nor that Drăghici's estate included Cican/Illea's 1/20 share. Exact parcel/boundary comparison is required.

sources.title: BNaR inventory no. 3447, cotă 138: Listă de întărituri de documente referitoare la moșia Iurghiceni
sources.source_type: archival finding aid / digitized archive document
supports: BNaR preserves a dedicated list of title-confirmation documents concerning the Iurghiceni estate
Inventory number 3447 and archival quota 138 identify the item
sources.notes: This is a high-priority finding aid for reconstructing older Iurghiceni title history. The catalogue entry itself does not expose the list's internal contents, so no underlying deed date or Cican connection is claimed until the document is recovered and read.

sources.title: BNaR Iurghiceni dossier, cotă 134–137: Grigorcea/Filip, Vasco-Costin-Iacob, Băsărăbești shares and fragmentary property list
supports: cotă 134: Grigorcea son of Sava, grandson of Iosip of Tătărani, transfers his Iurghiceni share to priest Filip
cotă 135: shares of brothers Vasco, Costin and Iacob in Iurghiceni
cotă 136: Băsărăbești shares belonging to Iurghiceni
cotă 137: fragmentary list of Iurghiceni property shares
sources.notes: These neighbouring catalogue items form a high-value branch map around the Iurghiceni title-confirmation list at cotă 138. Catalogue metadata alone does not establish whether any branch contains the 1547 Cican/Cicican–Illea share. The exact parcel boundaries and underlying deeds must be recovered before identities or continuity are asserted.

sources.title: BNaR Iurghiceni branch control: Vasco-Costin-Iacob shares and 1669 Vasco descendant transaction
supports: BNaR no. 3444/cotă 135 records shares of brothers Vasco, Costin and Iacob in Iurghiceni
BNaR I/214 (30 Nov 1669) records Constantin son of Vasile of Iurghiceni, grandson of Vasco cel Bătrîn, selling an Iurghiceni share
sources.notes: The two records are a research collision, not a proven continuous family branch. Patronymics, chronology, parcel fractions and boundaries must be compared before merging Vasco identities. No connection to the 1547 Cican/Cicican–Illea share is established.

sources.title: BNaR early Iurghiceni control sequence, 1497–1547
supports: I/3 (1497) and I/4 (1498) are earlier records in the same archival series but concern other properties/localities rather than a Cican Iurghiceni share
I/5 (26 May 1547) is the first currently identified Iurghiceni charter in this sequence naming Cican/Cicican and his son Illea
sources.notes: The sequence provides a catalogue-level negative control for the 1497–1547 interval. It does not prove that no earlier Iurghiceni Cican existed; uncatalogued or differently indexed records may remain.

sources.title: BNaR I/227–I/239, 1673 Iurghiceni title, share-selection and boundary dossier
supports: I/227: list of Iurghiceni estate documents
I/228: list of 19 purchase deeds for Iurghiceni and Doroșcani
I/229a-b: Iurghiceni situation and lists of property shares/boundaries
I/231a-c: lists of shares selected for the various răzeși when Iurghiceni was delimited
I/232, I/235 and I/239: further selection, staking and boundary records
sources.notes: This dossier is the strongest later source family for translating historical fractional ownership into identifiable parcels. It may preserve the documentary ancestry of later shares, but the inventory metadata alone does not establish that any listed share descends from the 1547 Cican/Cicican–Illea 1/20. Manuscript contents must be recovered before making that connection.

sources.title: BNaR I/245–I/259, 1676–1680 Iurghiceni/Băsărăbești transaction chain
supports: 1676 I/245: Ionașco Cămăraș and Toader Vîrnav recover Iurghiceni/Doroșcani shares after a pledge to Constantin Ciuta
1677 I/246: Ionașco, son-in-law of Pantiliti, and Anușca daughter of Pantelei sell a share from the Băsărab pillar in Iurghiceni
1677 I/247: Vasile Clineș and wife sell one-quarter of Pantelei's share from the Băsărab pillar
1679 I/249: Crăciun and relatives sell one-third of paternal inheritance from the Băsărăbești pillar
1680 I/256 and I/258: Irina daughter of Obreja and Urîta daughter of Nastasia, granddaughter of Obreja, sell inherited Iurghiceni shares
sources.notes: This chain materially strengthens the Băsărăbești/share-fraction continuity test. It does not establish a connection to Cican/Illea.

sources.title: DRH A Moldova XXV, 15 and 22 July 1639: Obrejie son of Agahia acquires Băsărăbești-side Iurghiceni shares
sources.publisher: Documenta Romaniae Historica, A. Moldova, vol. XXV
supports: 15 July 1639: Irina daughter of Mărica Nehoe, granddaughter of Băsărabă, and Niță vătah sell their Iurghiceni share from the Băsărăbești side to Obrejie son of Agahia, nephew of priest Gavril, for 50 zlotys
22 July 1639: Vasile son of Andreica and Constantin son of Ana, grandsons of Borcea, sell their Băsărăbești-side Iurghiceni share to the same Obrejie son of Agahia for 35 zlotys
sources.notes: This independently strengthens the 1591–1592 Obrejie son of Agafia branch because the 1639 buyer has the same distinctive patronymic/relationship cluster. It is a branch-continuity result, not evidence that Obrejie descends from Cican/Illea.

sources.title: 1637 Obrejie son of Lupu and 1644 Miron of Iurghiceni for deceased son Obrejie
sources.source_type: published primary-document evidence / BNaR digitized holdings
supports: 1637 May 26: Obrejie son of Lupu appears as a man of Iurghiceni giving testimony concerning a payment to Buhuș
1644 Nov 28: Miron of Iurghiceni donates his selected Iurghiceni share, including a house-place and pond-place, for the soul of his deceased son Obrejie
sources.notes: Potentially important identity/kinship bridge within the Obrejie-Miron cluster, but the 1637 Obrejie son of Lupu, the 1632 Obrejie associated with Miron, and the deceased Obrejie son of Miron in 1644 are not merged. Exact documentary wording and intervening records are required.
